title: Progressive traffic escrow & rollback orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a rollout orchestrator that introduces a traffic escrow concept: hold a configurable fraction of traffic in an escrow pool during progressive releases, release it only after safety gates pass, and use escrow to accelerate rollbacks without cold-starting baseline models. Deliver a rollout specification DSL that supports traffic splits, step schedules, shadow multiplexing, and automated rollback policies driven by statistical tests and business guards. The orchestrator must integrate with the Console (rollout UI + trace links), the Serving Runtime (routing/preview endpoints), and telemetry pipelines (latency, error-rate, model-quality metrics). Backwards compatible API mappings should allow existing rollout configs to be migrated without downtime.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout spec DSL supports: initial traffic split, ordered steps, step dwell durations, escrow fraction, shadow routes, and fallback model mapping
Runtime implements escrow routing: escrowed requests are routed to baseline and candidate appropriately and do not count toward customer visible traffic until released
Auto-rollback triggers based on configurable SLOs and statistical tests (e.g., non-inferiority with minimum sample size) and performs rollback within the target SLO window
Console shows per-step health, escrow size, and provides manual release/abort controls with audit trail
E2E test harness validates stable rollouts for synthetic workloads (latency P95, error spikes, and quality regression detection) and simulates capacity-constrained scenarios
Migration script converts legacy progressive rollout configs to new DSL with no traffic disruption
Documentation & API schema published and reviewed by SDK/Docs team
Security review completed (if flagged) and KMS/HSM interactions documented
tasks: Design DSL syntax and examples (milestone: v0 spec)
Prototype escrow routing in serving runtime (feature-flagged)
Implement auto-rollback engine with pluggable detectors (latency/error/quality)
Console integration: rollout timeline, step controls, and audit log entries
Telemetry: add rollout-id tagging to spans and metrics, expose step-level dashboards
Create migration utility for existing rollout configs
Write E2E integration tests including shadow traffic and induced failures
Run staged field trial with non-critical internal models before public rollout

notes: Trade-off: escrow increases request duplication for safety (baseline + candidate) until released — cost vs. rollback speed must be tuned per tenant.
Alternative considered: sticky gradual ramp (session-based) but rejected due to cross-tenant traffic patterns and difficulty guaranteeing minimum sample sizes for statistical tests.
Decision: use combination of classical statistical tests + heuristics (min sample, sustained delta) to reduce false positives for rollback.
Follow-up: evaluate integrating model-quality signals from Redwood Optimize to trigger automated rollbacks based on eval set regressions.
Risk: interaction with Dedicated capacity burst policies — coordinated testing required to avoid eviction during rollback windows.
